newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Bildt says Sweden PM cowardly for EMU silence - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bildt says Sweden PM cowardly for EMU silence - paper.

text.p: Swedish opposition leader Carl Bildt critisised Prime Minister Goran Persson of being cowardly for wavering on membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), daily newspaper Dagens Nyheter said on Tuesday.
"Persson should long ago have taken a public stance on EMU," Bildt said after he was thanked by European Union foreign ministers for his services as international peace coordinator in Bosnia.
Bildt, leader of the conservative Moderates Party in Sweden, has stepped down from his Bosnia post and was replaced by former Spanish foreign minister Carlos Westendorp on May 30.

The ruling Social Democrats will announce their view on EMU membership at 1430 GMT on Tuesday after being tightlipped about their own opinions, instead pointing to polls showing Swedes have a fairly hostile attitude to EMU membership.
"This is a strange way of acting," Bildt said.
"You might just as well step back and wait for Sunday's survey by (pollster) Sifo.
"A prime minister must say what he thinks, take responsibility for that and have the courage and boldness to lead the country, even if times are rough."
The Social Democrats' popularity has slumped in the polls this year to the lowest levels since April 1991 while public opposition to EMU remains high.

The Social Democrats are expected to reject joining EMU in 1999 but leave the door open for possible membership in a few years time. This is partly due to the low public opinion for EMU memberhips and internal disagreements about participation.
"The prime minister should lead the nation and never sacrifice the interests of the country and the prime minister's capacity in order to keep his divided party together," Bildt said.
